Access parts of an f_outliers result with $

Source: R/foutliers.R
cash-.f_outliers.Rd

An f_outliers result is a list of tables: output_df when one column was checked, or one table per checked column. $ gives these tables by name, as usual. In addition, a column of the outlier table can be taken directly from the result: bad_rows$row_id returns the flagged row numbers (with several checked columns: all flagged rows), and with one checked column any column of its table works, for example bad_rows$biomass_g. A name that is not part of the result stops with an error that lists what is available, instead of returning NULL silently. Use [[ for the standard list behaviour.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'f_outliers'
x$name

Arguments

x

An object of class f_outliers.

name

The name of a result table or of a column in the outlier table.

Value

A data frame (a result table) or a vector (a column).

Examples

bad_rows <- f_outliers(biomass_g ~ treatment, data = plant_trial)
bad_rows$row_id       # the flagged row numbers
#> [1] 21
bad_rows$output_df    # the full outlier table
#>   row_id biomass_g treatment block plant_id time_weeks height_cm
#> 1     21      64.6     low_N    B2      P07          6      50.3
#>   chloroplast_count infected
#> 1                43       no
